filename: When and where soil dryness matters to ecosystem photosynthesis_.pdf
title: When and where soil dryness matters to ecosystem photosynthesis
testbed_rationale: The study applies diagnostic machine learning and explainable AI attribution techniques to existing eddy covariance and satellite datasets to evaluate driver sensitivities rather than constructing parameterization or emulator benchmark datasets.
pain_points: Strong covariation and negative correlation between soil moisture and vapour pressure deficit via land-atmosphere feedbacks under water-limited conditions.
Confounding effects from incoming radiation and air temperature.
Traditional feature attribution techniques (like SHAP) fail by assuming predictor independence, which does not hold across distinct causal regimes (energy-limited vs water-limited).
High computational cost of computing causal Shapley values due to combinatorial calculations.
Lack of global in situ observational root-zone soil moisture measurements.
extraction_notes: LEAP-affiliated paper (Pierre Gentine funded via LEAP AGS-2019625). Explores causal attribution of ecosystem water limitations on photosynthesis.
